the appellant was under a prohibition order arising from a prior firearm conviction

crime_highlights: the appellant, Stephen Logan, was operating his motor vehicle, driving home from a tavern when the vehicle left the road, and ended up in a creek
The appellant’s cousin and friend, Eric Noah, who was a passenger in the vehicle drowned and another passenger, the appellant’s brother, was seriously injured.
The sample contained 193 milligrams of alcohol per 100 litres of blood.
rationale_highlights: this court must consider whether a reformatory sentence to be served in the community is an appropriate alternative to incarceration in a penitentiary

the learned trial judge erred in principle in the sentencing of the appellant by not giving adequate weight to the facts of the appellant being an aboriginal, his unique and important role in his small Reserve community and to the principles of restorative justice
alcohol abuse is often prevalent within aboriginal communities given the many inequities and injustices faced by members of those communities
note: 1999 Gladue-era appeal; conditional sentence of 20 months substituted.
